content: Ketoconazole can increase the levels or effects of nateglinide by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Nefazodone can elevate ketoconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and ketoconazole can similarly increase nefazodone levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended in both cases. Ketoconazole raises nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Similarly, ketoconazole increases neomycin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, requiring caution and monitoring. Ketoconazole elevates netupitant/palonosetron levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. While netupitant is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4, no dosage adjustment is required. However, caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole also increases nicardipine and nifedipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. For nifedipine, ketoconazole reduces its metabolism, further increasing its levels. Ketoconazole raises nilotinib levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are advised. Similarly, ketoconazole increases nimodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Ketoconazole also elevates nintedanib levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, necessitating close monitoring and potential therapy modification. If adverse effects occur, dose reduction, therapy interruption, or discontinuation may be required. Nirmatrelvir increases ketoconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. When co-administered with ritonavir, ketoconazole's dose should not exceed 200 mg/day. Similarly, nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases ketoconazole levels, requiring dose limitation and close monitoring. Ketoconazole raises nitrendipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. It also increases norgestrel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may heighten the risk of adverse effects. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors can increase systemic norgestrel concentrations, requiring caution and monitoring. Both ketoconazole and ofloxacin prolong the QTc interval, necessitating close monitoring and therapy modification. Ketoconazole increases oliceridine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required, with close monitoring for respiratory depression and sedation. If the inhibitor is discontinued, oliceridine dosage may need to be increased to achieve stable effects. Ketoconazole elevates ondansetron levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, but no dosage adjustment is recommended. However, caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole increases osilodrostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring therapy modification and dose reduction of osilodrostat by half when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ketoconazole raises ospemifene levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Similarly, ketoconazole increases oxybutynin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Ketoconazole also elevates oxycodone levels, warranting therapy modification and potential dose reduction when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ketoconazole increases paclitaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Similarly, ketoconazole raises paliperidone levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition and prolongs the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring and therapy modification. Ketoconazole elevates panobinostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is necessary, with a reduced starting dose of 10 mg for panobinostat when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ketoconazole also increases parecoxib levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Ketoconazole raises paricalcitol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Similarly, ketoconazole increases paromomycin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, necessitating caution and monitoring. Both ketoconazole and paroxetine prolong the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring and therapy modification. Ketoconazole and pazopanib both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and monitoring. Ketoconazole increases perampanel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Similarly, ketoconazole elevates phenytoin levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Ketoconazole raises pimozide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. It also increases pioglitazone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating caution and monitoring. Ketoconazole increases pitavastatin toxicity through OATP1B1 inhibition, which may heighten the risk of myopathy. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ketoconazole elevates polatuzumab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, and MMAE, a CYP3A4 substrate. Ketoconazole increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition and prolongs the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring and therapy modification. Ketoconazole also increases pravastatin toxicity through OATP1B1 inhibition, heightening the risk of myopathy. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ketoconazole raises praziquantel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Similarly, ketoconazole increases prednisolone and prednisone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein inhibition, requiring caution and monitoring. Ketoconazole elevates progesterone levels (intravaginal gel, micronized, and natural forms) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. It also increases propafenone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, requiring caution and monitoring. Ketoconazole raises quetiapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is necessary, with a reduced quetiapine dose to one-sixth of the original when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ketoconazole also increases quinine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating caution and monitoring. Ketoconazole elevates quizartinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is required, with a reduced dose of 4 mg/day during co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. After discontinuing the inhibitor, resume the previous quizartinib dose. Ketoconazole raises rabeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Similarly, ketoconazole increases ramelteon levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, requiring caution and monitoring. Rifabutin decreases ketoconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Similarly, rifampin reduces ketoconazole levels by increasing its metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Ketoconazole elevates rifaximin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, necessitating caution and monitoring. It also increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, but no rilpivirine dose adjustment is required. Monitor for breakthrough fungal infections when azole antifungals are co-administered with rilpivirine. Ketoconazole raises riociguat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and other mechanisms, necessitating therapy modification and close monitoring. Reduce the riociguat dose to 0.5 mg TID when initiating treatment with strong CYP and P-gp/BCRP inhibitors. Ketoconazole increases ripretinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Ketoconazole elevates risperidone levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition and prolongs the QTc interval, necessitating close monitoring and therapy modification. It also increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein, requiring caution and monitoring. Ketoconazole raises roflumilast levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Similarly, ketoconazole increases romidepsin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein inhibition, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring and therapy modification. Ketoconazole elevates sacubitril/valsartan levels through OATP1B1 inhibition, necessitating caution and monitoring. Ketoconazole raises saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is necessary, with a reduced saxagliptin dose of 2.5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.
